what: Where a single Supabase Storage POST stops being accepted on the preview branch, measured directly rather than inferred, on 20 September 2026. This is the transport the product uses for every upload.
whyItMatters: The owner's gVCF ceiling is 8 GiB. Issuance grants a lease for a file that size, and the bytes then cannot arrive.
whatTheProductSends: src/lib/uploads/subject-upload-browser.ts sends the file as ONE XMLHttpRequest POST to /storage/v1/object/genomes/<stagingKey>, which is Supabase's standard upload. The product implements neither resumable (TUS) nor S3 multipart.
documented: Supabase's own documentation: standard uploads can transfer up to 5 GB; resumable and S3 uploads support up to 50 GB. The project's global file size limit (9 GB here) governs what Storage will keep, not what one request may carry.

inTheBrowser.result: net::ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED after 328.2 s and 320.1 s, no HTTP response, and no entry for the request in the branch's edge log.
inTheBrowser.whatThePersonSees: The page's own progress stops at 'Uploading to private storage… 25%' about twenty seconds in and never moves again; five and a half minutes later the upload is reported as failed, with no mention of size. The browser keeps sending after the edge has already refused, so the 413 never reaches it.

sentDirectly.how: One streamed POST of the same file to the same endpoint with the service-role key and no browser, through the same egress path, so the browser is out of the question.
sentDirectly.body: 413 Payload Too Large, served by Cloudflare, so the refusal is made at the edge in front of Storage on the declared Content-Length.

accepted.observed: no refusal; the transfer began and was aborted on purpose after 8 s having sent 796,983,296 bytes
no refusal; aborted after 4 s having sent 382,402,560 bytes
no refusal; aborted after 4 s having sent 283,508,736 bytes

whereTheRefusalStarts.reading: The boundary lies between 5,242,880,000 bytes and 5,368,708,096 bytes, which is the documented 5 GB. Every accepted probe was aborted deliberately within seconds; none of them left an object in the bucket, which was checked afterwards.
whereTheRefusalStarts.note: The probe bodies were sparse zero files, so nothing about their content reached the bucket, and no fixture or personal data was involved.

consequence: A gVCF ceiling above about 5 GB cannot be met by this product until the uploader gains a resumable or multipart path. Setting the ceiling higher only moves the failure later: the lease is granted, the person waits out the whole transfer, and the refusal that does arrive says nothing about size.
